results.Summary: Southeast Toyota Distributors, LLC (SET) is recalling certain 2017-2019 Toyota Camry, Corolla, Rav4, Sienna, and Yaris iA vehicles equipped with factory-installed floor mats. results.Summary: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (Toyota) is recalling certain 2019 Camry vehicles. The Occupant Classification System (OCS) may have been improperly calibrated, which may prevent the proper deployment of the front passenger air bag and knee air bag, in the event of a crash.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 208, "Occupant Crash Protection."
results.Consequence: In the event of a crash, if the air bags do not deploy as designed, the front seat passenger has an increased risk of an injury.
results.Remedy: Toyota will notify owners, and dealers will recalibrate the OCS, free of charge.  The recall began August 27, 2019.  Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-888-270-9371.  Toyota's number for this recall is K0M.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Southeast Toyota Distributors, LLC (SET) is recalling certain 2017-2019 Toyota Camry, Corolla, Rav4, Sienna, and Yaris iA vehicles equipped with factory-installed floor mats. results.Consequence: An incorrect label may lead to unintentionally overloading the vehicle, increasing the risk of a crash.

results.Summary: Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing (Toyota) is recalling certain 2019 Camry vehicles. The Occupant Classification System (OCS) may have been improperly calibrated, which may prevent the proper deployment of the front passenger air bag and knee air bag, in the event of a crash.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 208, "Occupant Crash Protection."
results.Consequence: In the event of a crash, if the air bags do not deploy as designed, the front seat passenger has an increased risk of an injury.
results.Remedy: Toyota will notify owners, and dealers will recalibrate the OCS, free of charge.  The recall began August 27, 2019.  Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-888-270-9371.  Toyota's number for this recall is K0M.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Remedy: Toyota will notify owners, and dealers will recalibrate the OCS, free of charge.  The recall began August 27, 2019.  Owners may contact Toyota customer service at 1-888-270-9371.  Toyota's number for this recall is K0M.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

The insured driver's reported symptom of complete brake pedal depression with no stopping force is a textbook presentation of hydraulic vacuum brake assist failure, directly matching the recalled defect. The police report assigns 100% fault to the other/manufacturer party with zero fault attributed to the insured, meaning the pure comparative negligence doctrine applies at full recovery factor (1.0) with no reduction. With a rules-engine demand of $12,250, a recovery floor of $8,575, and a 90% probability of recovery, the claim is strongly positioned for active pursuit against Toyota. The statute of limitations deadline remains 896 days away, providing ample time to file, but early action is advisable to preserve evidence and witness availability.
risks: Toyota may argue the recall repair was available and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the remedy, asserting a failure-to-mitigate defense that could reduce or eliminate manufacturer liability.

Toyota's defense team may challenge causation by claiming the brake failure was due to independent wear, deferred maintenance, or a separate mechanical issue unrelated to the recalled vacuum assist component.
Toyota may contend that the insured or a third-party mechanic modified or serviced the brake system in a way that supersedes the recall defect as the proximate cause of the failure.
The manufacturer may dispute the sufficiency of the police report's fault assignment, arguing it reflects only officer opinion and not a formal engineering or accident-reconstruction finding.

Toyota may invoke a comparative fault argument at trial by introducing evidence of the insured's speed, following distance, or reaction time, even though the rules engine currently assigns 0% insured fault, this could reduce the net recovery below the $12,250 demand.
